subject: maths

concepts.title: Conditional Probability
concepts.definition: The chance of an event taking place given that a related event from the same experiment has already occurred.
concepts.key_idea: Restricting the sample space to outcomes where the given condition has already taken place.
question_patterns: find the conditional probability of event E given event F
calculate P(E|F) when P(E ∩ F) and P(F) are given
what is the probability of event A given that event B has occurred
determine the likelihood of event E occurring given event F
evaluate conditional probability P(A|B)

solution_steps.action: divide intersection probability by given event probability
solution_steps.explain: apply conditional probability formula P(E|F) = P(E ∩ F) / P(F)

concepts.title: Properties of Conditional Probability
concepts.definition: Rules establishing how conditional probabilities behave regarding total space, complementary sets, and unions.
concepts.key_idea: Conditional probabilities inherit standard probability axioms over the reduced sample space.
question_patterns: verify that P(S|F) equals 1
show that P(E'|F) is equal to 1 minus P(E|F)
find the conditional probability of the complement event
determine P((A union B)|F) for disjoint events
check the properties of conditional probability for given events

solution_steps.explain: subtract P(E|F) from 1 to obtain P(E'|F)

concepts.title: Multiplication Theorem on Probability
concepts.definition: Principle stating that the joint probability of consecutive events equals the initial event probability times the subsequent conditional probability.
concepts.key_idea: Finding joint probabilities through sequential stage-by-stage conditioning.
question_patterns: find the joint probability of events E and F
calculate P(E ∩ F) using the multiplication theorem
determine the probability of both events occurring sequentially
compute P(A and B) given P(A) and P(B|A)
evaluate the probability of drawing two items without replacement

solution_steps.action: multiply initial probability by conditional probability
solution_steps.explain: use multiplication theorem P(E ∩ F) = P(E) * P(F|E)

concepts.title: Independent Events
concepts.definition: Pair of events where knowing whether one happens provides no information about the likelihood of the other.
concepts.key_idea: Joint probability of independent events is simply the product of individual probabilities.
question_patterns: check if events A and B are independent
calculate P(A ∩ B) for independent events
find the joint probability when events are independent
determine whether two given events are statistically independent
evaluate P(A and B) given independent probabilities

solution_steps.explain: for independent events P(A ∩ B) = P(A) * P(B)

concepts.title: Theorem of Total Probability
concepts.definition: Summing conditional path probabilities across mutually disjoint hypotheses that exhaust the entire outcome space.
concepts.key_idea: Computing total marginal probability by summing weighted path probabilities across a sample space partition.
question_patterns: calculate the total probability of an event A
find P(A) across two exhaustive mutually exclusive hypotheses
determine the total likelihood of an outcome given initial path probabilities
evaluate overall probability using the theorem of total probability
compute the overall chance of an event from partition probabilities

solution_steps.explain: multiply prior P(E1) by conditional P(A|E1)
multiply prior P(E2) by conditional P(A|E2)
add path probabilities to obtain total P(A)

concepts.title: Bayes' Theorem
concepts.definition: Mathematical procedure for revising initial belief probabilities about causes after receiving new empirical evidence.
concepts.key_idea: Calculating the updated posterior probability of a cause given an observed outcome.
question_patterns: find posterior probability using Bayes theorem
calculate P(E1|A) given prior and likelihood values
determine the probability that a cause occurred given the observed result
compute posterior likelihood of hypothesis E1 after event A
apply Bayes theorem to find conditional probability of a partition event

solution_steps.explain: multiply prior P(E1) by conditional P(A|E1)
sum joint probabilities for all partition branches

solution_steps.action: divide numerator by total probability denominator
solution_steps.explain: calculate posterior probability P(E1|A) = num / den
